records.title: Modification of cutaneous blood flow by skin application of homeopathic anti-inflammatory gels
records.source: STP Pharma Sciences 1999:219–222 (French, no DOI, no free PDF)
records.why: The closest record anyone has found to what S-685 asks for: homeopathic anti-inflammatory preparations measured by laser Doppler velocimetry of skin blood flow. The design is a methyl-nicotinate-induced vasodilation on the forearm, inhibited by pre-treatment with homeopathic gels under patches, with percentage inhibition against vehicle. It is not a Heel combination product (the agents are Urtica urens, Apis, Belladonna and Pulsatilla) and not injected, so it does not answer S-685's letter; it does show the method has been applied to homeopathy, in a French pharmaceutical-sciences journal that PubMed does not index.

records.title: Treatment of Sports Injuries with Traumeel Ointment: A Controlled Double-Blind Study (Ambruš)
records.why: A Heel product (Traumeel S and Traumeel Sine ointment) in a placebo-controlled trial of 102 outpatients in three arms whose co-primary outcomes were regression of swelling and reduction in skin temperature — a skin-perfusion proxy. The skin-temperature outcome was null: 'With respect to the main criteria of skin temperature, no differences became apparent among the three treatment groups', while swelling and all secondary outcomes favoured both Traumeel forms over placebo. Topical ointment, not an injectable, and the journal is not recorded in the index.

records.title: [Cutaneous blood flow following subcutaneous infiltration of lidocaine with and without the addition of adrenaline or ornipressin]
